# `Tea.Tui.Ui`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Tea.Tui.Ui — the Tui shape's view surface.

A `tui` program's `view` returns `Screen msg`, a type distinct from the web
`Element msg`: putting a web builder into a `Screen` view is a compile-time
type error (IPE-T0001), never a silent drop.

The builders take this module's OWN `Attribute msg`, which exposes only
terminal-honorable, cell-native attributes (spacing/padding in whole cells,
horizontal alignment, bold/underline text style, and terminal-palette
colours). DOM-only attributes (`Ui.onClick`, `Ui.scrollbars`, `Ui.inFront`,
…) are simply not in this type, so naming one in a `Screen` view is a type
error rather than an attribute the renderer quietly discards. Terminal input
(keys) arrives through subscriptions (`Ipe.Tea.Tui.Sub`), not view attributes.

## `none`

```ipe
none : Screen msg
```

An empty screen view — renders nothing.

## `text`

```ipe
text : String -> Screen msg
```

`text str` — a single line of text.

## `cells`

```ipe
cells : List (List Char) -> Screen msg
```

`cells grid` — a raw terminal cell grid.  Each inner list is one row of
characters; the terminal backend paints it verbatim.  The one place the
word "cells" survives in the surface: the raw-grid escape hatch.

## `el`

```ipe
el : List (Attribute msg) -> Screen msg -> Screen msg
```

`el attrs child` — wrap a single `Screen msg` child with attributes.

## `row`

```ipe
row : List (Attribute msg) -> List (Screen msg) -> Screen msg
```

`row attrs children` — lay out `Screen msg` children horizontally.

## `column`

```ipe
column : List (Attribute msg) -> List (Screen msg) -> Screen msg
```

`column attrs children` — lay out `Screen msg` children vertically.
